title: Israel's Near-Daily Gaza Strikes Kill Five More as West Bank Violence Surges
excerpt: An Israeli airstrike killed two Palestinians in northern Gaza on Thursday, while three others were shot dead in the West Bank amid escalating settler violence that now causes more than half of all Palestinian injuries in the occupied territory.
body:
• Israeli airstrikes killed two Palestinians in northern Gaza on Thursday; three more were shot dead in the West Bank in separate incidents
  • Over 1,160 Palestinians have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire, with at least 57 killed in the week of July 13–20 alone, according to OHCHR
  • Settler violence in the West Bank has surged to more than three attacks per day in 2026, accounting for 55% of all Palestinian injuries this year

An Israeli airstrike killed two Palestinians in northern Gaza on Thursday, while three others were shot dead in the occupied West Bank, according to Palestinian authorities, medics, and the Israeli military. The deaths came amid what the United Nations has called an intensification of Israeli military operations that has killed dozens in recent days.

Israel's military said it had targeted militants in the Gaza strike, according to Reuters. In the West Bank, an Israeli military official said a civilian — an apparent reference to a settler — killed two Palestinians after they stabbed and wounded an Israeli during a dispute near the village of Beit Furik. A third Palestinian was shot by Israeli forces after a separate stabbing attack that wounded a soldier.

Nine Months of Ceasefire, Near-Daily Strikes

More than nine months after a U.S.-backed ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took effect in October 2025, Israel continues to launch near-daily airstrikes across the Gaza Strip, claiming to target Hamas militants. The fragile truce has failed to halt the violence.

https://x.com/MOSSADil/status/2080420192778105238

More than 1,160 Palestinians and four Israeli soldiers have been killed since the ceasefire began, according to Palestinian and Israeli tallies respectively. Palestinian medics say most of the dead are civilians. The UN's Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights has verified the killing of 685 Palestinians between October and mid-April, including 283 women and children.

"The whole of the Gaza Strip is under the Israeli occupation. Human rights of the Palestinians ought to be respected, the Israeli occupation has to end and a fair, durable two-State solution has to be implemented."

— Thameen Al-Kheetan, OHCHR spokesperson

From July 13 to 20 alone, the Israeli military killed at least 57 Palestinians, including six children and eight women, according to OHCHR. Among the victims, 34 were killed far from the Israeli-imposed "yellow line" — painted concrete blocks Israel has installed across the Strip to mark the edge of its military control.

A Shrinking Strip, a Growing Death Toll

On Tuesday, an Israeli airstrike on the Sabra neighbourhood of Gaza City killed Firas Al-Masri, his wife Salsabeel, and their four children as they slept, according to Reuters. The Israeli military confirmed the strike, saying it had targeted a Hamas militant and was still assessing the outcome.

Days earlier, an airstrike killed at least eight Palestinians and wounded 20 others attending a funeral in Nuseirat refugee camp, Gaza health officials said. Hamas condemned that strike as a "brutal massacre."

Conflict monitor ACLED reported that Israeli airstrikes against Hamas and other militants rose to more than 40 in June, the highest monthly total since the ceasefire. Meanwhile, the Palestinian population in Gaza remains trapped in an ever-shrinking area as Israel moves the yellow line westward, with the military now controlling approximately 70% of the strip, according to reports on the stalled ceasefire deal.

West Bank Settler Violence at Record Levels

The violence extends well beyond Gaza. Israeli settler attacks have become the leading cause of Palestinian injuries in the occupied West Bank, accounting for 55% of all cases in 2026, according to the UN's relief coordination office OCHA.

The rate of settler-linked injuries has risen sharply — from one injury every three days in 2020 to more than three per day so far in 2026. Between July 7 and 13, about 65 Palestinians, including 18 children and 10 women, were injured by Israeli forces or settlers.

In the Hiwara community south of Yatta in Hebron, settlers physically assaulted farmers and sprayed them with pepper spray in five separate attacks, injuring 45 Palestinians including 12 children. About 700,000 Israeli settlers live among 2.7 million Palestinians in the West Bank and East Jerusalem. Most foreign governments consider the settlements illegal under international law.

Humanitarian Crisis Deepens

A UN-backed food security report released this week warned that two-thirds of Gaza could face acute hunger by year-end. While supplementary feeding programmes served 12,000 pregnant and breastfeeding women earlier this year, that number had halved to 6,000 by May, with further reductions expected due to funding shortfalls, according to Reuters.

Health infrastructure is also buckling. The World Health Organization and its partners on Monday evacuated nine child patients and their 15 companions to Jordan and one adult patient to Turkey for medical treatment unavailable in Gaza. Since October 2023, over 12,700 patients have been evacuated abroad for treatment, the UN spokesperson said.

Diplomatic Stalemate

The 20-point ceasefire plan remains stalled. Key elements of the agreement — including a complete end to fighting and an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza — remain unrealised. An international force meant to secure parts of the strip has yet to materialise. Hamas recently offered to dissolve its Gaza government to pave the way for a breakthrough, but Israel has continued expanding its military footprint across the territory.

The UN has urged third states to take urgent action to ensure full respect for the ceasefire and accountability for violations. For the more than two million Palestinians in Gaza, the gap between the ceasefire on paper and the reality on the ground continues to widen.
nri_angle: The intensifying violence and stalled ceasefire carry implications for Indian diaspora communities in the Gulf and the broader Middle East, while India's diplomatic balancing act between Israel and Palestine faces renewed pressure.
